title: Payment-method pressure is a scam warning
summary: The FTC warns that unexpected demands for bank transfers, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, payment apps, or gift cards are strong scam indicators.
impersonates: A government agency, business, prize administrator, or other trusted organization
warningSigns: Unexpected contact demanding payment
Only one hard-to-reverse payment method is accepted
Pressure to act before you can verify
actionSteps: Do not send the payment
Search the person or organization independently
Use a credit card when appropriate
Contact the payment company immediately if money was sent
responseScript: I will verify this independently before making any payment.

title: Fake IC3 recovery agent
summary: The FBI warns that scammers impersonate IC3 or FBI personnel and promise to recover money already lost to fraud.
impersonates: The FBI or Internet Crime Complaint Center
warningSigns: Claims recovered funds are waiting
Moves the conversation to social media or Telegram
Uses AI-generated official-looking videos
Directs you to a lookalike IC3 website
actionSteps: Stop communicating
Type ic3.gov directly into the browser
Do not pay a recovery fee
Report the impersonating account and website
responseScript: IC3 does not contact people on social media or charge to recover funds.

title: Treatment-center search impersonation
summary: The FTC warns that paid search ads can use another treatment center’s name while displaying an impersonator’s phone number and website.
impersonates: A substance-use treatment center or recovery helpline
warningSigns: A paid ad uses the clinic name but a different website or phone number
The caller answers with a generic greeting
The caller avoids confirming the exact facility
actionSteps: Scroll past paid search results
Type the known treatment center address directly
Verify the phone number through an independent source
Report deceptive practices to the FTC
responseScript: Before sharing health information, I will confirm I reached the exact facility.

title: Military debt-forgiveness scam
summary: The FTC warns that callers invent military debt-forgiveness programs, claim ties to trusted institutions, and demand fees before providing help.
impersonates: A military bank, credit union, credit bureau, or veterans program
warningSigns: An unsolicited caller offers exclusive military debt forgiveness
The company wants an upfront fee
You are told to pay the company instead of your real creditors
actionSteps: Do not pay upfront
Contact the lender directly
Use military or VA financial counseling resources
Research the company with your state attorney general
responseScript: I will contact my lender directly before changing any debt payment.

title: Fake job offer and reshipping work
summary: Scammers pose as employers, conduct convincing remote interviews, and may ask new hires to buy equipment, move money, or receive and reship packages.
impersonates: An employer or recruiter
warningSigns: The recruiter uses a personal email or text-only interview
You must pay for equipment or deposit a check
The job requires receiving and reshipping packages
The offer arrives before identity and references are verified
actionSteps: Verify the employer through its official website
Search the recruiter and company independently
Never pay to get a job
Do not deposit a check and send money onward
responseScript: I will verify this job through the company’s official website before sharing information or money.

title: Fake rental listing
summary: The FTC warns that scammers copy or invent housing listings, advertise below-market rent, prevent tours, and demand hard-to-reverse payments.
impersonates: A landlord, property manager, or military housing contact
warningSigns: The rent is far below comparable properties
The landlord will not allow an in-person tour
The same address appears under another landlord or price
Payment must be cash, gift card, cryptocurrency, or wire transfer
actionSteps: Search the address independently
Tour the property or ask a trusted local person to visit
Verify the owner or manager
Do not use hard-to-reverse payment methods
responseScript: I will verify the property and landlord before signing or paying.

title: Unclaimed life insurance inheritance letter
summary: The FTC warns about letters from fake law firms claiming a person with your last name left a life insurance fortune.
impersonates: A lawyer or law firm
warningSigns: A stranger says you are heir to a policy worth millions
The sender proposes splitting the money
The sender asks for Social Security, bank, or payment information
actionSteps: Do not respond
Do not send money or personal information
Share the warning with family
Report the letter to the FTC
responseScript: I do not send information or money to strangers promising an inheritance.

title: Pet emergency and animal charity impersonation
summary: The FTC warns that scammers use stolen or AI-generated animal images to fake pet emergencies, charities, and prizes.
impersonates: Animal control, an animal hospital, shelter, or charity
warningSigns: A caller claims to have your missing pet and demands payment
Images of a distressed animal cannot be independently verified
A prize requires a payment
Only gift card, payment app, cryptocurrency, or wire transfer is accepted
actionSteps: Slow down and contact the organization directly
Reverse-image-search the pictures
Do not pay to collect a prize
Report the scam to the FTC
responseScript: I will verify the animal hospital, shelter, or charity independently.

title: Malicious website redirect chain
summary: The FBI warns that criminal traffic-distribution systems redirect advertisements, compromised sites, or phishing links to fake logins, financial scams, and malware.
impersonates: A legitimate website, login page, advertisement, or software update
warningSigns: A link or ad redirects through several unfamiliar domains
A familiar page appears at a slightly different URL
A website unexpectedly prompts a software update or login
actionSteps: Close the page
Navigate to the known website directly
Keep software and plugins updated
Use strong passwords and two-factor authentication
responseScript: I will close this page and navigate to the service directly.

title: Travel booking and fake toll scams
summary: The FTC warns that paid search ads can impersonate airlines or hotels and that fake unpaid-toll texts pressure travelers to pay.
impersonates: An airline, hotel, travel company, or toll agency
warningSigns: A paid result uses a familiar company name with a different URL or phone number
A text claims an unpaid toll and demands immediate payment
The seller accepts only wire transfer, gift card, payment app, or cryptocurrency
actionSteps: Type the company or toll agency website yourself
Check the URL and contact information
Research the offer before paying
Report the attempt to the FTC
responseScript: I will contact the travel company or toll agency through its official website.

title: Vacant-land owner impersonation
summary: Criminals forge IDs and impersonate owners of vacant parcels to list and sell property without permission.
impersonates: A vacant-land owner
warningSigns: Seller insists on a remote transaction
Price is unusually low
Identity documents do not withstand independent checks
Seller avoids video or in-person verification
actionSteps: Property owners should set title or tax alerts
Realtors should verify identity independently
Contact the recorded owner through separate records
Alert the title company and law enforcement
responseScript: I will verify the owner outside the contact information they supplied.

title: Crypto investment cash courier
summary: The FBI warns about fraudulent investment platforms that send couriers to collect cash from victims, often older adults.
impersonates: A romantic contact, investment expert, or cryptocurrency platform
warningSigns: Unsolicited investment relationship
A platform displays profits you cannot withdraw
Someone asks to collect cash at your home
A code or dollar-bill serial number is used to authenticate a courier
actionSteps: Do not meet the courier
Stop sending money
Preserve messages and account information
Contact your bank and report the scheme to IC3
responseScript: Legitimate investments do not send strangers to my home to collect cash.

title: Jury-duty arrest threat
summary: The FTC warns about callers using fake warrants and threats of arrest for supposedly missing jury duty.
impersonates: A U.S. Marshal, local police officer, or court
warningSigns: Threatens immediate arrest
Sends an official-looking warrant by text or email
Demands payment by app, crypto, gift card, or wire
actionSteps: Hang up
Do not use contact details in the message
Contact the court through an official government website
Report the attempt to the FTC
responseScript: Courts do not demand payment by phone. I will verify this directly.

title: Health insurance search-ad impersonator
summary: The FTC warns that paid search results can mimic government health insurance or Medicare websites to collect information, fees, or misleading enrollments.
impersonates: HealthCare.gov, Medicare, or another government health program
warningSigns: The first result is labeled Ad or Sponsored
A supposed government website does not end in .gov
The site asks for an unnecessary fee or routes you to an unexpected seller
actionSteps: Scroll past paid results
Check the complete URL
Type HealthCare.gov or the known official address yourself
Report deceptive ads to the FTC
responseScript: I will use the official .gov website instead of a paid search result.

title: Fake CAPTCHA installs malware
summary: The FTC warns that a fake CAPTCHA may tell users to run keyboard commands that paste and execute hidden malware.
impersonates: A browser security or human-verification prompt
warningSigns: A CAPTCHA asks you to press Windows plus R
The prompt tells you to paste commands or press Enter
A download begins after the verification
actionSteps: Do not run the commands
Disconnect from the internet if you complied
Run a security scan
Change passwords and enable two-factor authentication from another device
responseScript: Real CAPTCHAs do not ask me to run commands on my device.

title: Fake FTC employee photo ID
summary: The FTC warns that scammers text official-looking photo identification while impersonating agency employees to obtain money or account access.
impersonates: A Federal Trade Commission employee
warningSigns: An unexpected contact sends an FTC photo ID
The person asks for money or access to financial accounts
The contact uses the badge image as proof instead of independent verification
actionSteps: Stop communicating
Do not use contact information the sender provided
Verify through FTC.gov
Report the impersonation
responseScript: I will verify an agency contact using the official agency website.

title: Medicare hospice enrollment fraud
summary: Recruiters enroll people who do not need hospice, sometimes without their knowledge, so providers can bill Medicare.
impersonates: A hospice provider or Medicare helper
warningSigns: Free services conditioned on hospice enrollment
Gift card or cash offered for enrollment
Unknown hospice appears on a Medicare statement
actionSteps: Do not share Medicare information with unsolicited callers
Review Medicare Summary Notices
Check providers with Medicare
Report unknown services
responseScript: I will discuss hospice only with my doctor and a provider I verify.

title: Fake FIFA and World Cup websites
summary: The FBI warns that criminals spoof FIFA websites and advertisements to steal credentials, personal information, or payments around the 2026 World Cup.
impersonates: FIFA or a World Cup service
warningSigns: The domain is not exactly fifa.com or an official subdomain reached from it
A search advertisement redirects to another address
The page uses low-quality copied graphics or asks for sensitive information
actionSteps: Type www.fifa.com directly
Use a saved bookmark rather than an advertisement
Do not share information on an unverified page
Report the fake domain to IC3
responseScript: I will begin at the official FIFA website and verify the complete domain.

title: Cryptocurrency kiosk payment demand
summary: The FBI warns that scammers direct victims to withdraw cash, scan a supplied QR code, and send cryptocurrency through a kiosk.
impersonates: A government office, utility, company, lawyer, investment adviser, or acquaintance
warningSigns: An online-only contact directs you to a cryptocurrency kiosk
Someone supplies a QR code and detailed deposit instructions
A caller stays on the phone while you withdraw cash or operate the kiosk
The caller says cryptocurrency is the only payment
actionSteps: Do not withdraw or deposit the cash
Do not scan a QR code supplied by the caller
Contact the claimed organization directly
Report the scheme to IC3 and your financial institution
responseScript: No legitimate government or law-enforcement official demands payment at a cryptocurrency kiosk.

title: Social media account reverification phishing
summary: Messages claiming a verified social account has violated rules or must be reverified send users to fake forms that steal credentials or install malware.
impersonates: A social media platform
warningSigns: The message threatens immediate suspension
The link opens a different domain
A form asks for a password or recovery code
An attachment or download is presented as an appeal
actionSteps: Open the platform directly instead of the link
Check account notices inside the official app
Do not share passwords or one-time codes
Report and delete the message
responseScript: I will check my account inside the official app instead of using this link.

title: Publishers Clearing House prize-fee scam
summary: Impostors claim you won a Publishers Clearing House prize, then demand taxes, processing fees, gift cards, cash, or account information before releasing nonexistent winnings.
impersonates: Publishers Clearing House or a prize administrator
warningSigns: You are told you won without entering
Payment is required before receiving the prize
The caller requests gift cards, cash, cryptocurrency, or bank information
Secrecy or urgency is emphasized
actionSteps: Do not pay to claim a prize
Contact the organization through its official website
Do not share bank or identity information
Report the impersonation to the FTC
responseScript: A real prize does not require me to pay first.

title: Planning and zoning permit payment phishing
summary: The FBI warns that criminals use real public permit details while impersonating city or county officials and sending fraudulent fee invoices.
impersonates: A city or county planning and zoning department
warningSigns: The message contains accurate permit details but comes from a non-government domain
A PDF invoice says to request payment instructions only by email
Payment is requested by wire, peer-to-peer app, or cryptocurrency
The message threatens permit delays
actionSteps: Check the sender’s complete domain
Call the city or county using its official website number
Do not rely on seals or official names as proof
Report the email and invoice to IC3
responseScript: I will call the permitting office using the number on its official website.

title: IRS refund or account-verification message
summary: Emails, texts, direct messages, and QR codes impersonate the IRS and lead to fake account or refund pages.
impersonates: The Internal Revenue Service
warningSigns: Unexpected IRS message with a link or QR code
Threat or refund promise designed to create urgency
Page asks for tax, identity, or banking details
actionSteps: Do not open the link or attachment
Go to IRS.gov directly
Forward suspicious email to phishing@irs.gov
Review your IRS Online Account independently
responseScript: I do not use links in unexpected IRS messages.

title: AI-generated IRS phone threat
summary: Robocalls and cloned voices spoof IRS caller ID, demand immediate payment, or threaten arrest.
impersonates: The Internal Revenue Service
warningSigns: Urgent prerecorded threat
Caller ID appears to say IRS
Demand for immediate payment or secrecy
actionSteps: Hang up
Do not trust caller ID
Verify through IRS.gov
Report the call
responseScript: The IRS generally contacts taxpayers by mail first. I will verify independently.

title: Disaster and tragedy charity impostor
summary: Fraudsters exploit disasters and tragedies with fake charities that collect donations and personal information.
impersonates: A charity or disaster-relief organization
warningSigns: High-pressure request tied to a current tragedy
Donation requested by gift card, crypto, wire, or payment app
Charity cannot be found in official records
actionSteps: Search the IRS tax-exempt organization tool
Donate through the charity's official site
Do not send payment under pressure
Report the fundraiser
responseScript: I will verify the charity before donating.

title: Viral tax-credit or refund hack
summary: Social posts promote false deductions or credits that can cause refund delays, audits, penalties, or prosecution.
impersonates: A tax expert or successful taxpayer
warningSigns: Promises a secret refund method
Tells everyone they qualify
Encourages invented income, withholding, or expenses
actionSteps: Check the claim on IRS.gov
Ask a credentialed tax professional
Do not sign an inaccurate return
Correct a filed return promptly
responseScript: A viral post is not tax advice. I will verify the rule.

title: IRS Online Account setup helper
summary: Criminals pose as helpers to collect identity information or take over an IRS Online Account.
impersonates: An IRS account helper
warningSigns: Unsolicited offer to create an IRS account
Request for login, verification code, or identity documents
Link does not lead to IRS.gov
actionSteps: Create the account only at IRS.gov
Never share a one-time code
Change credentials if shared
Review tax records for identity theft
responseScript: I will set up my IRS account directly at IRS.gov.

title: Bogus self-employment tax credit promoter
summary: Promoters market a broad self-employment credit, charge fees, and encourage ineligible or inaccurate refund claims.
impersonates: A tax credit specialist
warningSigns: Promises a large guaranteed refund
Bases fees on the refund amount
Will not explain the legal eligibility rule
actionSteps: Check eligibility on IRS.gov
Use a credentialed preparer
Reject guaranteed-refund claims
Keep copies of all filings
responseScript: I will verify any tax credit with an independent professional.

title: Ghost tax-return preparer
summary: A paid preparer refuses to sign the return or include a valid preparer tax identification number, leaving the taxpayer responsible.
impersonates: A tax professional
warningSigns: Refuses to sign the return
Will not provide a PTIN
Asks you to sign a blank return
Directs the refund to another account
actionSteps: Check the preparer's credentials
Review the full return before signing
Use the IRS preparer directory
Report misconduct
responseScript: I will not file until the preparer signs and provides a valid PTIN.

title: Fabricated withholding refund scheme
summary: Promoters tell taxpayers to invent wages or withholding on tax forms to manufacture a refund.
impersonates: A tax strategist or preparer
warningSigns: Claims made-up withholding creates free money
Uses forms unrelated to your actual income
Says the IRS cannot verify the amounts
actionSteps: Do not file false information
Compare every form with real records
Consult a credentialed preparer
Amend an inaccurate return
responseScript: I will only report withholding shown in my real records.

title: Fake tax client document request
summary: Tax professionals and businesses receive fake new-client emails or document links that deliver malware and steal client data.
impersonates: A new tax client or business contact
warningSigns: Unexpected tax documents or cloud-sharing link
Sender domain does not match the claimed person
Pressure to open a file before speaking
actionSteps: Verify the sender by another channel
Do not enable macros or install software
Scan files in an isolated workflow
Reset credentials after suspicious access
responseScript: I will verify the sender before opening tax documents.

title: Tax-debt Offer in Compromise mill
summary: High-pressure companies overpromise tax-debt settlements and charge people who are unlikely to qualify.
impersonates: An IRS tax-debt resolution service
warningSigns: Guarantees pennies-on-the-dollar settlement
Demands a large fee before reviewing finances
Claims special access to the IRS
actionSteps: Use the free IRS pre-qualifier
Check professional credentials
Get the fee and service in writing
Avoid guaranteed outcomes
responseScript: I will check IRS eligibility before paying a tax-relief company.

title: Stolen-identity tax refund
summary: Criminals use stolen names and Social Security numbers to file tax returns and divert refunds.
impersonates: A taxpayer filing a legitimate return
warningSigns: IRS says more than one return used your SSN
Tax record lists an unknown employer
Unexpected tax transcript, notice, or refund
actionSteps: Create and secure an IRS Online Account
Respond to IRS identity-verification letters
File Form 14039 when directed
Secure credit and email accounts
responseScript: I will use IRS.gov directly to address possible tax identity theft.

title: Online romance turns into a money or crypto request
summary: A new online romantic partner builds trust, then asks for emergency money or steers the victim to a cryptocurrency investment.
impersonates: A romantic partner or investment mentor
warningSigns: Never meets reliably in person
Asks for secrecy or urgent financial help
Directs you to an unfamiliar investment platform
Profits appear but withdrawals fail
actionSteps: Stop sending money
Save messages and transaction records
Contact the financial institution
Report to IC3 and the platform
responseScript: I do not send money or invest for someone I only know online.

title: Counterfeit discount postage
summary: Online sellers offer deeply discounted Forever stamps that are counterfeit and may cause mail to be rejected.
impersonates: The U.S. Postal Service or an approved postage seller
warningSigns: Stamps discounted 20 to 50 percent
Bulk offer from an unknown third-party site
Seller cannot be verified as an approved provider
actionSteps: Buy from USPS or an approved provider
Avoid deep-discount social ads
Keep purchase records
Report counterfeit postage
responseScript: I will buy postage from USPS or an approved provider.

title: SEC social-media or text impersonator
summary: Fraudsters impersonate SEC staff to push stock tips, demand advance fees, or promise to recover investment losses.
impersonates: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
warningSigns: Unsolicited investment recommendation from an SEC profile
Recovery offer requiring a fee
SEC seal or real employee photo used as proof
actionSteps: Do not send money or identity documents
Verify staff using SEC.gov contact information
Check investments and professionals independently
Report the account
responseScript: The SEC does not endorse investments or charge to recover my money.

title: Fake online store blames tariffs
summary: Fraudulent online stores take payment, never deliver, then blame tariffs or customs and demand extra fees instead of providing a valid shipment or refund.
impersonates: An online retailer, carrier, or customs office
warningSigns: The price is unusually low
Tracking never becomes verifiable
The seller blames tariffs or customs and asks for more money
The shop has no independent reputation or reachable support
actionSteps: Research the seller before buying
Pay by credit card when possible
Verify tracking with the carrier directly
Dispute charges for goods that never arrive
responseScript: I will verify the seller and shipment independently before paying another fee.

title: Mail check washing
summary: Thieves steal mailed checks, erase or replace the payee and amount, and deposit altered or counterfeit versions.
impersonates: A legitimate check recipient
warningSigns: A mailed check never reaches the recipient
Check image shows a changed payee or amount
Unexpected duplicate or counterfeit check clears
actionSteps: Use secure online payment when possible
Mail checks inside a Post Office near pickup time
Review bank images promptly
Report altered checks to the bank and USPIS
responseScript: I will verify the cleared check image and report alterations immediately.

title: Fake Social Security benefit increase
summary: Messages promise a benefit increase or COLA activation and lead to fake SSA sites that steal identity and financial information.
impersonates: The Social Security Administration
warningSigns: Unexpected offer to activate extra benefits
Link to a non-SSA website
Request for payment or banking information
actionSteps: Do not click or respond
Go directly to ssa.gov
Check your my Social Security account
Report the message to SSA OIG
responseScript: Social Security increases do not require payment or an unsolicited helper.

title: Government badge or credential photo
summary: Impostors send real or doctored badge images to create trust before demanding money or personal information.
impersonates: Federal law enforcement or an inspector general
warningSigns: Sends a badge photo as proof
Threatens action unless you pay
Claims secrecy is required
actionSteps: Stop responding
Verify through an official agency number
Do not transfer money
Preserve and report the messages
responseScript: A badge photo does not verify a caller. I will contact the agency directly.

title: USPS package-tracking text
summary: USPIS warns that unsolicited package texts containing unfamiliar links are smishing attempts designed to steal personal or financial information.
impersonates: The United States Postal Service
warningSigns: You did not request text tracking
The message contains an unfamiliar link
The text claims a delivery needs payment or personal information
actionSteps: Do not click or reply
Track the parcel by typing USPS.com yourself
Forward the text to 7726
Send USPS-related smishing reports to spam@uspis.gov
responseScript: I will check tracking directly at USPS.com.

title: Fake USPS delivery-failure email
summary: USPIS warns that fake USPS emails use delivery-failure or unpaid-postage claims to spread malware and steal credentials or financial information.
impersonates: USPS or the Postmaster General
warningSigns: An unexpected delivery email contains a link or attachment
The message requests personal information or money
The email demands immediate action or contains poor grammar
actionSteps: Do not click or download
Forward USPS-related spam to spam@uspis.gov
Delete the email
Contact your financial institution if you interacted with the link
responseScript: I will check delivery information directly through USPS.com.

title: Fake process server and court case
summary: Callers claim a process server is looking for you or that a court case or debt requires immediate payment, using threats and incomplete case details to create panic.
impersonates: A court, process server, law firm, or debt collector
warningSigns: The caller threatens arrest or immediate service
No court name or verifiable case number is provided
Payment is demanded to stop legal action
The caller refuses written validation
actionSteps: Do not pay during the call
Contact the named court using its official website
Ask a debt collector for written validation
Report abusive collection attempts
responseScript: I will verify any case directly with the court before discussing payment.

title: Urgent computer security pop-up
summary: A fake Microsoft, Apple, or security alert tells you to call a number, then sells bogus support or seeks remote access.
impersonates: A technology or security company
warningSigns: Pop-up says to call immediately
Caller wants remote computer access
Payment requested for an invented infection
actionSteps: Do not call the pop-up number
Close the browser or restart the device
Run trusted security software
Contact support through the official company site
responseScript: Real security pop-ups do not tell me to call a phone number.

title: Unexpected package brushing scam
summary: USPIS warns that unsolicited packages may support fake reviews and can include QR codes leading to phishing sites.
impersonates: A retailer or third-party seller
warningSigns: A package arrives that nobody ordered
The parcel has no useful return address
A card asks you to scan a QR code to identify the sender
A review appears under your name for the item
actionSteps: Do not pay for unsolicited merchandise
Do not scan enclosed QR codes
Change account passwords and monitor credit
Report fake reviews to the retailer
responseScript: I will not scan a code or pay for merchandise I did not order.

title: QR-code phishing
summary: USPIS warns that fraudulent QR codes in messages, public places, or unsolicited packages can lead to fake sites that steal personal and financial information.
impersonates: A bank, government agency, company, or gift sender
warningSigns: An unexpected QR code urges immediate scanning
A code is pasted over another code in a public place
An unsolicited package asks you to scan to identify the sender
The destination requests login, Social Security, card, or PIN information
actionSteps: Do not scan unexpected codes
Navigate to the organization directly
Contact the impersonated organization
Report USPS-related quishing to spam@uspis.gov
responseScript: I will use the organization’s official app or website instead of this QR code.

title: Postal inspector voice-phishing call
summary: USPIS warns that callers spoof official numbers, threaten arrest, and impersonate Postal Inspectors to demand money or personal information.
impersonates: A Postal Inspector, USPS employee, or law-enforcement official
warningSigns: The caller threatens arrest or punishment
Caller ID displays an official-looking number
The caller asks you to confirm information they already know
Money or sensitive information is demanded immediately
actionSteps: Hang up
Do not confirm personal information
Call the agency using a verified number
Report postal impersonation to USPIS
responseScript: I will hang up and call the agency through its official website.

title: Familiar business account-problem message
summary: A message that appears to come from a known company claims an account problem or prize and directs you to a scammer.
impersonates: A bank, retailer, delivery company, or subscription service
warningSigns: Unexpected problem or prize
Link or phone number supplied in the message
Demand for gift card, crypto, or remote access
actionSteps: Do not click or call from the message
Open the company's app or known website
Check account activity independently
Report the impersonation
responseScript: I will contact the business using information I already trust.

title: Family emergency or grandparent call
summary: A caller impersonates a relative in trouble—sometimes with cloned audio—and demands immediate secret payment.
impersonates: A child, grandchild, lawyer, or police officer
warningSigns: Caller demands secrecy
Emergency cannot be independently confirmed
Payment requested by courier, wire, gift card, or crypto
actionSteps: Hang up
Call the relative on a known number
Ask a family verification question
Contact another family member
responseScript: I will call my family directly before sending anything.

title: Fake check and overpayment
summary: A stranger sends a check, often for too much, and asks you to return part before the bank discovers the check is fake.
impersonates: An employer, buyer, prize company, or client
warningSigns: Check exceeds the amount owed
You must send money, gift cards, or crypto back
Bank shows funds before the check is finally verified
actionSteps: Do not send any money onward
Contact the issuing bank independently
Tell your bank about the suspected fake
Report the sender
responseScript: Available funds do not prove a check is real.
